io.vidocq.runtime.extensions.jakartaee.web:vidocq-runtime-mansart-data-extension-codegen 0.4.0-RC2 发布, Companion codegen bundle for vidocq-runtime-mansart-data-extension.
        Declare this artifact in <annotationProcessorPaths> whenever the
        application depends on the Mansart Data extension.

        Pulls in:
          - mansart-data-processor : generates _Entity metamodel + *RepositoryImpl
            stubs + META-INF/mansart-repositories.list.
          - mansart-data-cdi       : hosts the BuildCompatibleExtension and the
            @Produces RepositoryRuntime. The APT classloader (isolated by Maven)
            must see the BCE; without it, the DeploymentValidator rejects every
            @Inject of a repository or of RepositoryRuntime.

io.vidocq.runtime.extensions.microprofile:vidocq-runtime-ravel-config-extension-codegen 0.4.0-RC2 发布, Companion codegen bundle for vidocq-runtime-ravel-config-extension.
        Declare this artifact in <annotationProcessorPaths> whenever the
        application depends on the Config extension; Maven resolves the transitive
        APT dependencies below automatically.

        Runs Ravel's Build Compatible Extension (ConfigCdiExtension) inside the Vauban
        processor, so the @ConfigProperty / @ConfigProperties beans it synthesises
        exist when the processor validates the deployment. Without it, every
        @Inject @ConfigProperty point fails the compilation as an unsatisfied

io.vidocq.runtime.extensions.microprofile:vidocq-runtime-cyrano-rest-client-extension-codegen 0.4.0-RC2 发布, Companion codegen bundle for vidocq-runtime-cyrano-rest-client-extension.
        Declare this artifact in <annotationProcessorPaths> whenever the
        application depends on the Rest Client extension; Maven resolves the transitive
        APT dependencies below automatically.

        - cyrano-cdi-vauban: runs Cyrano's Build Compatible Extension inside the Vauban
          processor, so the @RestClient bean of each @RegisterRestClient interface exists
          when the processor validates the deployment and is recorded for the runtime.
          Without it, @Inject @RestClient fails: the runtime does not run extensions over
          an application the processor already handled (unsatisfied dependency).
        - cyrano-processor: generates each client's proxy at compile time, so the
          application needs no `opens` to io.vidocq.cyrano.core (without it, Cyrano
          defines the proxy at run time, in the interface's package).

com.withorb.api:orb-kotlin-core 1.54.0 发布, Orb's API is built with the following principles in mind:

1. **Predictable developer experience**: Where applicable, the Orb API uses
   industry-standard patterns such as cursor-based pagination and standardized
   error output. To help with debugging in critical API actions, the API always
   strives to provide detailed and actionable error messages. Aliases such as
   external customer IDs aid in fast integration times.
2. **Reliably real time**: Orb's event-based APIs, such as event ingestion are
   designed to handle extremely high throughput and scale with concurrent load.
   Orb also provides a real-time event-level credits ledger and a highly
   performant webhooks architecture.
3. **Flexibility at the forefront**: Features like timezone localization and the
   ability to amend historical usage show the flexible nature of the platform.

You can download the latest OpenAPI spec
[here](https://api.withorb.com/spec.json) - pass `?version=3.0` for an OpenAPI
3.0-compatible spec.

io.vidocq.knock:knock-mp-health-api 0.4.0-RC2 发布, Re-package of org.eclipse.microprofile.health:microprofile-health-api with an explicit
        module-info.class (module name: microprofile.health.api). The official API only ships an
        Automatic-Module-Name, which prevents its direct use with jlink. This artifact is the sole
        source of the MP Health spec consumed by the Knock modules; the official TCK keeps using
        the upstream API.

        No upstream source file is vendored in this repository: the official .class files are
        unpacked from the upstream binary jar at build time, and the only source we own and compile
        is module-info.java. The upstream META-INF/LICENSE and META-INF/NOTICE are propagated
        verbatim into the produced jar, as required by Apache-2.0 section 4.
